mcqs.question: Which of the following numbers is incorrectly classified as a prime number?
mcqs.explanation: A prime number has exactly two distinct positive factors: 1 and itself. 2, 3, and 11 satisfy this condition. The number 9 has factors 1, 3, and 9, so it is composite, making option C the incorrect classification.

mcqs.question: Why is the number 1 not considered a prime number?

options.A: It has exactly one positive factor
options.B: It has more than two factors
options.C: It is divisible by every integer

mcqs.answer: It has exactly one positive factor
mcqs.explanation: Prime numbers are defined as natural numbers greater than 1 that have exactly two distinct positive factors, 1 and the number itself. The number 1 has only one factor (itself), so it does not meet the definition of a prime.

mcqs.learning_point: Find prime factors of a number
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the prime factorizations of 84 and 90?

options.A: Both have the same set of prime factors
options.B: 84 has a prime factor 7 while 90 does not
options.C: 90 has a prime factor 7 while 84 does not
options.D: Both numbers are powers of a single prime

mcqs.answer: 84 has a prime factor 7 while 90 does not
mcqs.explanation: 84 = 2² × 3 × 7, so 7 is a prime factor of 84. 90 = 2 × 3² × 5, which does not contain 7. Therefore option B is the correct comparison.

mcqs.question: If a number N can be expressed as N = 2³ × 3² × 5, how many positive divisors does N have?
mcqs.explanation: For a number expressed as p¹^a × p²^b × …, the total number of positive divisors is (a+1)(b+1)… . Here (3+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a prime number?

options.A: A natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive factors
options.B: A natural number that can be written as a product of two smaller natural numbers
options.C: Any number that is divisible by 1
options.D: A number that has only one factor

mcqs.answer: A natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive factors
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a prime number is a natural number greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and the number itself, i.e., exactly two distinct factors.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines a composite number?

options.A: A natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive factors
options.B: A natural number greater than 1 that has more than two distinct positive factors
options.C: A number that is divisible only by 1
options.D: A number that is a perfect square

mcqs.answer: A natural number greater than 1 that has more than two distinct positive factors
mcqs.explanation: A composite number has at least one divisor other than 1 and itself, giving it more than two distinct positive factors. Option B captures this definition.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly lists a prime number first and a composite number second?
mcqs.explanation: 7 is prime (only factors 1 and 7) and 9 is composite (factors 1, 3, 9). The other options either place a composite first or list two primes.

mcqs.question: When listing all factors of 12, which of the following numbers must always be included?
mcqs.explanation: Every positive integer has 1 as a factor, and the number itself is also a factor. Hence both 1 and 12 must appear in the factor list of 12. Zero is not a factor of any number.
